sections.heading: What is an automated concrete cube laboratory?
body: An automated concrete cube laboratory connects specimen preparation, controlled curing and compression testing through coordinated equipment and specimen records. REALJET configures the workflow around daily intake, test ages and available space. Laboratories receiving already-cast specimens can begin with curing and testing; producers casting their own cubes can include preparation.

sections.heading: How the specimen moves through the laboratory.
body: Fresh concrete enters the preparation cell from an agreed collection point. Filled moulds remain in initial storage until demoulding. Identified specimens move to curing, then to compression testing at the scheduled age. Moulds return through cleaning and preparation for the next batch.

sections.heading: Where should your laboratory begin?
body: The first automated stage depends on where specimens enter your workflow.

points.title: Ready-mix producers
points.text: Start with sample arrival and repeated cube preparation. Review peak batching periods, mix changes and washout alongside average daily volume.

points.title: Precast factories
points.text: Connect each cube to its production batch. Define the purpose of laboratory curing separately from any production element curing process.

points.title: Independent testing laboratories
points.text: Begin with specimen receipt, curing inventory and testing demand. Add a preparation cell only when the laboratory also casts specimens.

sections.heading: How much curing storage do you need?
body: For a steady intake held to a single test age, base storage equals groups received per day multiplied by days held. Multiply by specimens per group to estimate individual specimen positions. Mixed test ages need separate inventory calculations. Add peak intake, reserve space and access allowances before selecting the final configuration.
sections.note: Planning example only. The calculator estimates specimen inventory; it does not specify a machine rating or a guaranteed system capacity.

sections.heading: What determines the layout and project cost?
body: The estimate depends on specimen volume, curing method, the automation scope and the equipment already installed. Compare quotes against the same operating schedule and acceptance criteria. Include utilities, building interfaces, installation, training and maintenance access in the review.

faq: Do I need to automate the whole laboratory?

You can start with one work area. A preparation cell suits laboratories casting cubes; curing and robotic testing suit laboratories receiving already-cast specimens. REALJET reviews the handovers and provision for later stages before defining the scope.
Can the system handle cylinders or concrete cores?
The illustrated equipment uses 150 mm concrete cubes as its design basis. Cylinders, cores and other cube sizes need a separate review of moulds, gripping, storage and compression machine interfaces.
Can existing compression machines be retained?
An existing machine can be reviewed for reuse. REALJET needs its model, loading access, platen geometry, safety interfaces and available control or data connections before confirming compatibility.
How do manual and automated workflows differ?

A manual workflow relies on operators for mould handling, storage transfers and machine loading. An automated workflow assigns selected movements and schedules to equipment. Operators still manage sample acceptance, exceptions, maintenance and result review.
Is the feeding conveyor required?

The feeding route depends on the collection point. A local hopper may suit a nearby source. An elevated transfer route requires sufficient headroom, structural support and cleaning access. It is an optional part of the layout.
Does automation certify a laboratory or guarantee method compliance?

Laboratory accreditation and test-method compliance require their own documented procedures and verification. The selected method must be reflected in equipment settings, curing conditions, specimen handling and acceptance checks.

intro: Turn fresh concrete into identified test specimens through a controlled sequence of filling, compaction and finishing. Connect initial storage, demoulding and mould cleaning within the same preparation cell.
alt: Three-dimensional concrete cube preparation cell showing robots, preparation stations and initial storage racks

sections.heading: What does an automatic cube preparation cell do?
body: An automatic concrete cube making machine fills, compacts and finishes concrete in cube moulds within a coordinated preparation cell. Initial storage, demoulding and mould cleaning can be included in the specified workflow. REALJET configures the cell around the concrete mix, mould design and specimen schedule.

The cell coordinates mould positioning, concrete dosing, compaction and surface finishing. The preparation program is agreed around the concrete and test method, with station interlocks confirming each handover.

sections.heading: Bring the mould back ready for the next batch.
body: After the initial curing period, the demoulding station separates the specimen from the mould. The mould returns through cleaning and release-agent preparation; the selected mould design can include a bottom-paper station.

sections.heading: Keep cleaning and access in the layout.
body: Cleaning is part of the operating cycle. Collection trays, wash points and drainage routes need to remain accessible when the cell is operating. REALJET also plans access for nozzle, feeder and gripping-tool maintenance.

faq: Is demoulding included?
The preparation scope can include initial storage, demoulding and mould recycling. The agreed equipment list identifies which stations are included.
How many cubes can the machine make?
Capacity is specified for the selected mould, concrete, preparation sequence and operating shift. Send the daily and peak specimen workload so the cell can be sized correctly.
Can the cell handle different concrete mixes?
The material review covers workability, aggregate size, setting behavior and the required cleaning between batches. Special mixes need a defined validation sequence.
Does it include the fresh concrete supply line?
Supply can be local or connected through a separate feeding and transfer module. The collection point, transfer time and interface are agreed with the preparation layout.

sections.heading: How does concrete specimen curing automation work?
body: A concrete specimen curing system provides controlled curing conditions and organized storage until the scheduled test age. It combines the selected curing environment with specimen identification, location records and retrieval. REALJET sizes the storage and handling configuration from daily intake, retention time and the laboratory’s test schedule.

The project method determines the environment. Cabinet systems and controlled rooms provide different approaches to storage and access; existing water-curing facilities can be assessed for handling integration. REALJET defines the required conditions and monitoring before selecting the arrangement.

faq: Can we use our existing curing room?
REALJET reviews the room, storage positions, environment, access and handling route to determine what can be retained.
Does the cabinet include automated loading?
Environmental control and specimen handling are separate scope items. They can be combined, with the selected loading mechanism shown in the configuration.
Is one temperature and humidity setting suitable for every market?
The project method determines the required conditions. The configuration is specified for that method rather than a universal setting.
How do we size the system?
Provide daily specimen intake, group size, test ages, retained samples and peak workload. These inputs define the occupied inventory and usable storage requirement.

sections.heading: What does robotic compression testing automate?
body: A robotic concrete compression testing workstation combines a compression machine with specimen loading, transfer and result recording. The robot handles the agreed specimen movements while the testing machine applies the load. REALJET reviews machine access, specimen geometry, safety interfaces and data exchange together before specifying the workstation.
An automatic pressure machine controls the loading cycle. The workstation also coordinates specimen transfer, placement, guarding, result handover and removal of tested material.

faq: Can one robot serve multiple machines?
This can be evaluated against reach, guarding, test-cycle duration and access. The layout and handling schedule determine the practical arrangement.
Is dimensional measurement included?
It is a configurable workstation function. The quotation defines the measuring equipment, calibration and connection to the test record.
Can the workstation test cylinders or cores?
Those specimens need a separate handling and method review, including end preparation and gripping. They are not assumed to be covered by the cube configuration.
Who issues the test report?
The workstation supplies the agreed test records. Report review, approval and release remain part of the laboratory's quality process.
